newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares slumped 3.36 percent in one of their biggest ever one day falls, battered by options related selling after remarks from Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan pointing to higher US interest rates.
"There's been panic selling mainly out of the options market ahead of the expirations tomorrow," said one dealer. "The remarks from Greenspan have shaken out big sellers."

The AEX index of 25 leading Dutch shares closed 24.73 points down at 710.31, back up from a session low of 700.54. The index has dropped 70 points or nearly nine percent since it reached its 779.02 all-time high seven trading sessions ago on March 11.
Shares had plunged 1.50 percent at the opening on derivatives-related selling, doubling Wednesday's 6.69 point fall on increasing nervousness about a U.S. rate rise.

Greenspan's remarks on Thursday that the U.S. economy retained a "great deal of vigour" and that the jobs market was strong were taken as a signal the Federal Reserve was inching towards raising interest rates, possibly next week.

His remarks had a similar impact on the Dutch share market as his criticism last December of "irrational exuberance" in some financial markets. Those comments sparked an intra-day selloff of nearly 39 points in the AEX index.
Selling pressure built up on the options exchange to the point that exchange authorities suspended trading for 10 minutes shortly before the AEX close.
Computer-driven "programme" trades in shares and dealings in baskets of the 25 shares which make up the main AEX share market were also suspended, a spokesman for the exchange said.

Exchange figures show that Thursday's fall is the biggest one day fall in percentage terms since a 6.6 percent fall in October 1989, although that figure itself was dwarfed by the 12.00 percent drop on "Black Monday", October 19, 1987, the day that sparked a deep equity market slump around the world.
"There's still a lot of fear about interest rates, people are getting more and more nervous. Today's fall has got a lot to do with panic," one dealer said.

Analysts have for a while been saying the AEX was overvalued during its rise from 648 since the end of 1996. "It was already too high, but we knew that when it went through 750 and then through 770 that we had to be involved," said a dealer.

"This was a predictable correction, we could see the index back below the 700 level soon enough," he added. A recent Reuter poll of analysts' expectations for the AEX averaged at 712 for the end of 1997 although some had seen it as low as 680.
